recent_posts.title: AutoMapper 16.1.1 Released
recent_posts.summary: AutoMapper 16.1.1 is a patch release addressing two critical issues: a thread deadlock caused by Microsoft deprecating sync decryption APIs (fixed using a safer sync-over-async pattern), and a security vulnerability where cyclic or self-referential object graphs could trigger uncontrolled recursion during mapping, leading to stack exhaustion and potential denial of service. Users are urged to upgrade immediately.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper 16.1 and MediatR 14.1 Released
recent_posts.summary: Jimmy Bogard has released AutoMapper 16.1 and MediatR 14.1 as part of regular quarterly releases. AutoMapper 16.1 adds support for factories and conditions to use dependencies (previously limited to Func-based callbacks). MediatR 14.1 adds support for complex generic hierarchies and includes several bug fixes. Both packages are available on NuGet. AutoMapper also hit the milestone of 1 billion downloads.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper 16.0.0 and MediatR 14.0.0 Released with .NET 10 Support
recent_posts.summary: AutoMapper 16.0.0 and MediatR 14.0.0 have been released with .NET 10 support. Both libraries now align their major releases with .NET's release cadence to simplify dependency management. This release includes no API changes but adds NuGet package signing for enhanced security verification, confirming packages are published by Lucky Penny Software.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper 15.1 and MediatR 13.1 Released
recent_posts.summary: AutoMapper 15.1 and MediatR 13.1 have been released as part of a new quarterly release schedule. Both versions now include first-class support for .NET Framework 4.6.2 alongside the previously restored netstandard2.0 support, with builds and tests running on both Windows and *nix platforms. The releases include new features, enhancements, and bug fixes.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper and MediatR Roadmaps
recent_posts.summary: Jimmy Bogard outlines future development plans for AutoMapper and MediatR libraries following renewed commercial sponsorship. AutoMapper will focus on implementing source generators to improve debugging capabilities while maintaining its extensibility model and IQueryable support. MediatR development will move away from Microsoft DI container dependencies to enable advanced features like policy-based behaviors, result pattern support, and better integration with Blazor, Minimal APIs, and domain events. Both libraries have restored netstandard2.0 support to ease .NET Framework to .NET Core migrations.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper and MediatR Commercial Editions Launch Today
recent_posts.summary: Jimmy Bogard announces the launch of commercial editions for AutoMapper and MediatR libraries under his new company Lucky Penny Software. The libraries now use a dual-license model with both RPL (open source) and commercial options. Commercial licensing is tier-based by team size (1-10, 11-50, unlimited developers) with subscription pricing. A free Community edition is available for companies under $5M revenue, non-profits, educational use, and non-production environments. Existing versions remain under their original licenses, while new major versions require license acceptance and optional license keys.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper and MediatR Licensing Update
recent_posts.summary: AutoMapper and MediatR are transitioning to a dual licensing model to ensure their long-term sustainability. The new model will make these libraries free for OSS developers, individuals, hobbyists, non-profits, startups, and non-commercial use, while commercial entities will need to obtain paid licenses. The aim is to provide value beyond basic access and avoid per-seat licensing to make the process simpler. Pricing details and licensing tiers are still being determined, with plans to launch soon.

recent_posts.title: AutoMapper and MediatR Going Commercial
recent_posts.summary: To ensure the long-term sustainability of his OSS projects AutoMapper and MediatR, Jimmy Bogard is commercializing them. After leaving Headspring and starting his own consulting business, Bogard struggled to maintain his OSS contributions without the support he previously had. He aims to figure out a viable model that allows him to fund his time for OSS development, improve the projects, and build communities around them. While the details are not yet finalized, Bogard is committed to being transparent throughout the process.

recent_posts.title: MediatR 12.5.0 Released
recent_posts.summary: MediatR 12.5.0 introduces new features such as a convenience method to register open behaviors and improved cancellation token support, ensuring it is passed everywhere, including behaviors. Other cleanup items are also part of this minor release.

recent_posts.title: Upcoming Training on Modern .NET with Vertical Slice Architecture in Frankfurt
recent_posts.summary: A training event focused on Modern .NET with Vertical Slice Architecture will take place in Frankfurt on June 25th-26th. Participants can opt for a 2-day or 3-day course. The additional day will cover advanced topics like bounded contexts, messaging, integration patterns, microservices, and modular monoliths.
